title: SLA-Aligned Key Rotation & SIEM Ingest Playbook
content:
Purpose and scope
This playbook defines an operational, SLA-driven approach to cryptographic key rotation for Redwood Inference’s KMS/HSM/BYOK deployments and the associated SIEM ingestion and evidence automation. It covers regular rotations, emergency (zero-day) rotations, cross-checks with RBAC v2 policies, audit log schema expectations, and practical automation recipes to produce verifiable evidence for compliance reviews.

Why SLA alignment matters
Rotation cadence should be risk-informed, but operationally executable. Tying rotation schedules to SLAs (latency, availability, incident windows) minimizes business disruption while ensuring crypto hygiene. For example:
- Customer-sensitive BYOK keys: rotation window = quarterly (90 days) with a 48h maintenance SLA for in-place rollover.
- System root and cluster-level keys: rotation window = 180 days, with 72h SLA for safe transition and verification.
- Short-lived ephemeral signing keys for telemetry: rotation window = 24 hours (automated, no manual ops).

Key categories and recommended cryptoperiods (example)
- BYOK tenant master keys (customer-supplied): 90 days; automated rotation tools where customer permits; escrow snapshot before rotation.
- Tenant envelope keys (service-managed): 90–180 days depending on sensitivity label.
- Platform signing keys (deploy/CI): 30–90 days depending on exposure.
- HSM root/backup keys: 180–365 days; offline key ceremony required for root replacement.
- Ephemeral runtime keys (per-request or session): minutes–hours; strict TTL enforcement via KMS token gating.

SLA-driven rotation schedule template
Fields: key_id, category, current_cryptoperiod_days, desired_rotation_window_start (UTC), maintenance_sla_hours, rollback_window_hours, owner, runbook_ref
Sample line: KEY-tenant-43, BYOK, 90, 2025-02-01T02:00Z, 48, 4, priya.patel@redwood.ai, RBAC-check-pt1
Operational constraints: pick rotation windows that avoid peak cross-region traffic; prefer low-traffic regional maintenance windows; schedule canary tenant rotations first for wide rollouts.

Emergency rotation (zero-day) playbook
Trigger conditions: confirmed key compromise, HSM firmware exploit, unauthorized KMS API key exposure.
Immediate steps (first 2 hours):
1) Triage: incident responder tags the key_id and elevates to Security Incident Commander (SIC).
2) Freeze: Add temporary deny policy via RBAC v2 to prevent further use of the compromised key (policy id: deny-temp-<key_id>-<ts>).
3) Snapshot: force an evidence export (signed export manifest) — include HSM attestation blob, KMS operation log segment (last 24h), and active session list.
4) Rotate: generate replacement keypair in an isolated HSM slot or new tenant key in BYOK flow. Do not reuse parameters of compromised key.
5) Backfill: re-encrypt short-lived caches using the new key; for long-lived blobs schedule phased rewraps.
6) Postmortem evidence: ingest the signed export manifest into SIEM and attach to Jira incident.
Notes: prioritize containment over graceful transitions. Maintain a documented rollback path in case of automation failure.

RBAC v2 checks and pre-rotation gating
Before any rotation job runs, automation must validate:
- principal (service account or human) has rotate_key permission on the key resource per RBAC v2 policy binding.
- no active deny bindings exist for the key.
- service accounts that will receive access after rotation are pre-provisioned and validated.
Gating flow (simplified): automation -> query RBAC API -> get effective bindings -> assert rotate permission -> create pre-rotation approval ticket if human approval required.
Audit trail: record RBAC evaluation result (pass/fail), binding snapshot id, and ticket id as part of the rotation job payload.

SIEM ingestion and evidence schema (expected fields)
Objective: produce consistent, machine-searchable evidence for every rotation event that supports compliance queries and forensic timelines. Minimal ingest schema (flattened fields):
- event_id: unique string
- event_type: key_rotation | key_generation | key_export | key_compromise | rbac_eval
- key_id: canonical key locator (tenant:keyname:version)
- key_category: byok | envelope | platform | hsm_root | ephemeral
- initiator: principal id (svcacct: or user:)
- initiator_role: string (e.g., svc-infra-rotations)
- rbaceval_snapshot: snapshot id or null
- operation_mode: automatic | manual | emergency
- previous_key_version: string
- new_key_version: string
- rotation_start_ts: ISO8601
- rotation_end_ts: ISO8601 or null
- outcome: success | partial | failed
- failure_reason: short string or null
- hsm_attestation_blob_id: id or null
- evidence_bundle_url: signed URL or document id
- ticket_id: Jira- or Linear-like id
- region: cloud-region or onprem-site
- sla_window_hours: integer (as string)
- rollback_window_hours: integer (as string)
- retention_policy: days (as string)
- notes: freeform text
Example log line (JSON-as-string):
{"event_id":"evt-20250121-8a3f","event_type":"key_rotation","key_id":"tenant-7:envelope-2:v4","key_category":"envelope","initiator":"svcacct:rotations@redwood.ai","operation_mode":"automatic","rotation_start_ts":"2025-01-21T03:04:00Z","rotation_end_ts":"2025-01-21T03:05:10Z","outcome":"success","hsm_attestation_blob_id":"att-57b9","evidence_bundle_url":"gs://redwood-evidence/att-57b9.tar.gz","ticket_id":"JIRA-SEC-4421"}

Evidence automation pattern (recommended)
1) Rotation automation finishes -> assemble evidence bundle: rotation job manifest + RBAC snapshot + HSM attestation + config diffs + signed audit log segment.
2) Store bundle to immutable evidence store (object storage with WORM) and generate signed manifest (detached signature).
3) Emit SIEM event using the ingest schema above; include evidence_bundle_url and signature reference.
4) Trigger compliance workflow: attach evidence to Jira ticket, notify security-review Slack channel, and set review deadline based on key category.
Automation tips: use content-addressed storage naming (sha256) for bundles; store a human-friendly index document for quick lookup.

SIEM mapping guide (Splunk/Elastic examples)
- Splunk: index=crypto_evidence sourcetype=redwood:key_rotation | eval key_id=... | table event_id key_id initiator outcome hsm_attestation_blob_id evidence_bundle_url
- Elastic: use a dedicated index template with keyword mappings for key_id and event_type, date detection for rotation timestamps, and nested keyword for initiator. Keep the schema flat to simplify queries.

Retention and access controls for evidence
- Short-lived evidence (ephemeral keys): keep 30 days by default.
- Standard rotations: keep 365 days.
- High-sensitivity BYOK evidence: retain 7 years and mirror to cold archival store.
Access: evidence store read requests must be mediated by RBAC v2 and generate audit logs; evidence downloads for compliance review should create a signed one-time URL and attach the downloader identity to the SIEM event.

Testing and verification matrix
- Canary rotations: run on a non-critical tenant weekly to validate automation paths.
- RBAC fuzz tests: simulate permission drift by injecting temporary bindings and confirm gating prevents rotation jobs.
- SIEM ingest tests: inject synthetic events and confirm downstream alerts and dashboards trigger.
- HSM attestation replay: periodically re-verify that attestation blobs validate with vendor public keys.

Runbook checklists (operator-facing)
Pre-rotation checklist:
- Confirm maintenance window and ticket created.
- Verify RBAC evaluation passed and snapshot recorded.
- Ensure backup/escrow snapshot exists and is intact.
- Validate automation playbook version and hashes.
During rotation checklist:
- Monitor automation log stream for errors.
- Confirm SIEM event emitted with event_type=key_rotation.
- If partial failure, pause automation and escalate.
Post-rotation checklist:
- Verify downstream services switched to new key (health-check endpoints).
- Confirm evidence bundle stored and signature validated.
- Attach evidence to ticket and set review status to done.

Common failure modes and mitigations
- Failure: downstream service rejects new key (incompatible envelope algorithm). Mitigation: preflight compatibility checks and ability to rollback quickly to previous key version for up to rollback_window_hours.
- Failure: RBAC policy evaluation false-negative. Mitigation: include a secondary human-approval gate for high-sensitivity keys.
- Failure: SIEM ingestion lag. Mitigation: create local durable buffer and replay mechanism for events; mark ticket as evidence-pending.

Operational automation snippets (pseudocode)
- RBAC preflight: call rbac_api.evaluate(principal, action=rotate, resource=key_id) -> record snapshot_id
- Rotation job: spawn hsm.generate_key(slot=isolated) -> wrap new_key with wrapping_key -> update key metadata with new version -> emit siem_event(payload)
- Evidence bundle: tar(manifest.json, rbacsnap.json, attestation.bin) -> store://evidence/sha256 -> sign(bundle)

Open questions and decisions needed
- Cryptoperiod policy for cross-tenant shared secrets (currently undefined). Proposal: align to highest tenant SLA.
- BYOK escrow: decide whether escrow snapshots are encrypted with customer-provided secondary keys or platform escrow keys.
- HSM vendor attestation formats: normalise parsing code to handle vendor-specific blobs.

References and appendices
- Confluence: key-management-policy (CONFLUENCE-KEYFLOW-8732)
- Jira incident template: JIRA-SEC-4421
- Ops script repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/216
